title: CHAPTER 10: SPECIFIC BANKING AND FINANCIAL LAWS

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: FEMA 1999 replaced the stringent FERA 1973, shifting the regulatory emphasis from foreign exchange conservation to facilitation of external trade and payments.
The Banking Ombudsman Scheme was established under Section 35A of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949 to resolve customer complaints regarding banking service deficiencies.
Regional Rural Banks (RRBs) were constituted following the recommendations of the Narasimham Committee (1975) and governed by the RRB Act, 1976.
Equity in RRBs is jointly held by the Central Government (50%), the Sponsor Bank (35%), and the State Government (15%).
NABARD was established on July 12, 1982 under the NABARD Act, 1981 based on the recommendations of the CRAFICARD / B. Sivaraman Committee.

cells: Facilitate external trade and payments; promote orderly development and maintenance of foreign exchange market
FERA (Foreign Exchange Regulation Act), 1973 — civil penalties replaced criminal penalties; liberal regime
Free (liberalised); no prior RBI approval generally needed; subject to specific restrictions
Restricted; require RBI/FIPB approval; include FDI, FPI, borrowings, immovable property transactions
Bank or any other person authorised by RBI to deal in foreign exchange (AD Category I, II, III)
Civil offence (not criminal); penalty up to 3 times amount involved or Rs.2 lakh; ED investigates FEMA violations
Minor violations can be compounded (settled) by RBI or ED; reduces litigation
Resident individuals can remit up to USD 250,000 per financial year for any permitted current/capital account transaction
If FEMA violation proceeds from scheduled PMLA offence, ED can investigate under PMLA also

cells: All RBI-regulated entities: banks, NBFCs, payment system participants; complaints above Rs.20 lakh also accepted
Free; online at cms.rbi.org.in; Ombudsman award up to Rs.20 lakh; compensation for harassment up to Rs.1 lakh
Merged into IOS 2021; previously separate for NBFCs
Also merged into IOS 2021; covers UPI, prepaid instruments, etc.
SEBI Complaints Redress System; securities market complaints
Online; timeline-bound; insurer must resolve or IRDAI intervenes
Banking service deficiency; not refusal of loan (policy matter)
Not IBPS RRB exam focus but general awareness
Regional Rural Banks Act, 1976; RRBs set up under provisions of this Act
Government of India (50%) + State Government (15%) + Sponsor Bank (35%)
Provide banking and credit facilities to agriculture and other rural sectors; serve small farmers, artisans, landless labourers, small entrepreneurs
Notified area specified in establishment order; typically one or more districts within a state
National bank (public sector) that provides assistance: capital subscription, staff, training, management
Regulated and supervised by RBI + NABARD; NABARD inspects RRBs; NABARD provides refinance
Board of Directors; Chairman appointed by Central Government on recommendation of NABARD/Sponsor Bank
Authorised capital Rs.5 crore; paid-up capital as per establishment order; can be enhanced by Central Govt
Many RRBs amalgamated by Government to form stronger entities; consolidated from 196 (2005) to 43 (2024)

items: Remember the exact shareholding ratio in RRBs: Central Govt = 50%, Sponsor Bank = 35%, State Govt = 15%.
NABARD recommendation committee: CRAFICARD (B. Sivaraman Committee); RRB recommendation committee: Narasimham Working Group (1975).
FEMA non-compliance is treated as a civil offence, whereas offences under the repealed FERA were criminal offences.
Banking Ombudsman derives its statutory authority from Section 35A of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949.

cells: NABARD (National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development) established 12 July 1982 under NABARD Act, 1981
Credit functions (refinance); development functions; regulatory functions (supervises RRBs and cooperative banks)
Equal share between Central Govt and RBI (now Govt holds majority; RBI has transferred shares to Govt)
NABARD inspects RRBs under Section 35 of Banking Regulation Act, 1949 read with NABARD Act
Rural Infrastructure Development Fund; shortfall in PSL deposited to RIDF managed by NABARD; states get loans from RIDF for rural infrastructure
NABARD pioneered Self Help Group-Bank Linkage Programme from 1992; largest microfinance programme globally
